nodes.summary: The arithmetic expressions of IMP are built inductively from the constants $n$, one for each natural number $n$, and the variables $x_i$, one for each natural number $i$: if $a_1$ and $a_2$ are arithmetic expressions, then so are $a_1 + a_2$, $a_1 - a_2$ and $a_1 \cdot a_2$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic expressions of IMP

nodes.summary: The Boolean expressions of IMP are built inductively from the constants true and false and the comparisons $a_1 = a_2$ and $a_1 \le a_2$ of arithmetic expressions $a_1, a_2$: if $b$, $b_1$ and $b_2$ are Boolean expressions, then so are the negation $\neg b$ and the conjunction $b_1 \wedge b_2$.
nodes.title: Boolean expressions of IMP

nodes.summary: The big-step relation says when running a command $c$ from a state $s$ terminates in a state $t$; we then say that $c$ takes $s$ to $t$. It is the least relation satisfying the following rules. The command $\mathtt{skip}$ takes $s$ to $s$. The assignment $x := a$ takes $s$ to the state $s[x \mapsto a(s)]$, which agrees with $s$ except that $x$ has the value $a(s)$ of the arithmetic expression $a$ in $s$. If $c_1$…
nodes.title: Big-step semantics of IMP

nodes.summary: The commands of the while-language IMP are built inductively from skip and the assignments $x_i := a$ of an arithmetic expression $a$ to the variable $x_i$ with index $i \in \mathbb{N}$: if $c$, $c_1$ and $c_2$ are commands and $b$ is a Boolean expression, then so are the sequential composition $c_1 ; c_2$, the conditional if $b$ then $c_1$ else $c_2$, and the loop while $b$ do $c$.
nodes.title: Commands of IMP

nodes.summary: A configuration of IMP is a pair $(c, \sigma)$ of a command $c$ and a state $\sigma$.
nodes.title: IMP configuration

nodes.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$, $s_1$, $s_2$, if $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s_1$ and also terminates by small steps in $s_2$, then $s_1 = s_2$.
nodes.title: Small-step termination is deterministic

nodes.summary: For all IMP configurations $x$, $y$, $z$, if $x$ steps to $y$ and $x$ steps to $z$ in one small step, then $y = z$.
nodes.title: Determinism of IMP small-step semantics

nodes.summary: For every command $c$ and every state $s$, if $c$ run from $s$ terminates in a state $t_1$ and also in a state $t_2$ under the big-step semantics, then $t_1 = t_2$.
nodes.title: Determinism of IMP big-step semantics

nodes.summary: The truth value of a Boolean expression in a state $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is defined by recursion on the expression: the constants true and false have values true and false; for arithmetic expressions $a_1$ and $a_2$, the comparison $a_1 = a_2$ is true exactly when the values of $a_1$ and $a_2$ in $\sigma$ are equal, and $a_1 \le a_2$ is true exactly when the value of $a_1$ is at most the value of…
nodes.title: Evaluation of IMP Boolean expressions

nodes.summary: The value of an arithmetic expression in a state $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is the natural number defined by recursion on the expression: a constant $n$ has value $n$, the variable $x_i$ with index $i$ has value $\sigma(i)$, and for arithmetic expressions $a_1$ and $a_2$, the expressions $a_1 + a_2$, $a_1 - a_2$ and $a_1 \cdot a_2$ have as value the sum, the truncated difference and the product of the…
nodes.title: Evaluation of IMP arithmetic expressions

nodes.summary: For assertions $P$ and $Q$ on states and an IMP command $c$, the partial-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid if and only if, for all states $s$ and $s'$, whenever $P$ holds in $s$ and $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$, $Q$ holds in $s'$.
nodes.title: Hoare validity via small-step termination

nodes.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, if $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$: finitely many small steps lead from the configuration $(c, s)$ to $(\mathrm{skip}, s')$.
nodes.title: Big-step executions terminate in small steps

nodes.summary: Let $x = (c, s)$ and $y = (d, t)$ be configurations and $s'$ a state. If $x$ moves to $y$ in one small step and $d$ evaluates from $t$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.
nodes.title: Prepending one small step to a big-step execution

nodes.summary: Let $x = (c, s)$ and $y = (d, t)$ be configurations and $s'$ a state. If $x$ reaches $y$ in finitely many (possibly zero) small steps and $d$ evaluates from $t$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.
nodes.title: Prepending finitely many small steps to a big-step execution

nodes.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, if $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.
nodes.title: Small-step termination implies big-step evaluation

nodes.summary: A state of an IMP program is a function $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ assigning a natural-number value $\sigma(i)$ to each variable, where variables are identified by natural numbers $i$.
nodes.title: IMP program states

nodes.summary: The single-step relation $\to$ on IMP configurations is the smallest relation satisfying the following rules, for all variables $x$, arithmetic expressions $a$, Boolean expressions $b$, commands $c, c_1, c_1', c_2$ and states $\sigma, \sigma'$. Assignment: $(x := a, \sigma) \to (\mathtt{skip}, \sigma[x \mapsto v])$, where $v$ is the value of $a$ in $\sigma$. Sequencing:…
nodes.title: IMP small-step relation

nodes.summary: The relation $\to^*$ on IMP configurations is the reflexive, transitive closure of the small-step relation: $x \to^* y$ when $y$ is reached from $x$ by a finite sequence of zero or more small steps.
nodes.title: IMP multi-step relation

nodes.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$ if and only if $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.
nodes.title: Equivalence of small-step and big-step semantics

nodes.summary: A command $c$ terminates from an initial state $\sigma$ in a final state $\tau$ when the configuration $(c, \sigma)$ reaches $(\mathtt{skip}, \tau)$ in finitely many small steps.
nodes.title: Termination of an IMP command

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
